{{Short description|Study of structures where a subset must sum to zero}}

In mathematics, '''zero-sum Ramsey theory''' or '''zero-sum theory''' is a branch of [[combinatorics]]. It deals with problems of the following kind: given a [[combinatorial]] structure whose elements are assigned different weights (usually elements from an [[Abelian group]] <math>A</math>), one seeks for conditions that guarantee the existence of certain substructure whose weights of its elements sum up to zero (in <math>A</math>). It combines tools from [[number theory]], [[algebra]], [[linear algebra]], [[graph theory]], [[discrete analysis]], and other branches of mathematics.

The classic result in this area is the 1961 theorem of [[Paul Erdős]], [[Abraham Ginzburg]], and [[Abraham Ziv]]:<ref>{{cite journal | zbl=0063.00009 | last1=Erdős | first1=Paul | last2=Ginzburg | first2=A. | last3=Ziv | first3=A. | title=Theorem in the additive number theory | journal=Bull. Res. Council Israel | volume=10F | pages=41–43 | year=1961 }}</ref> for any <math>2m - 1</math> elements of <math>\mathbb{Z}_m</math>, there is a subset of size <math>m</math> that sums to zero.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Erdös-Ginzburg-Ziv theorem - Encyclopedia of Mathematics |url=https://encyclopediaofmath.org/wiki/Erd%C3%B6s-Ginzburg-Ziv_theorem |access-date=2023-05-22 |website=encyclopediaofmath.org}}</ref> (This bound is tight, as a sequence of <math>m - 1</math> zeroes and <math>m - 1</math> ones cannot have any subset of size <math>m</math> summing to zero.<ref name=":0" />) There are known proofs of this result using the [[Cauchy-Davenport theorem]], [[Fermat's little theorem]], or the [[Chevalley–Warning theorem]].<ref name=":0" />

Generalizing this result, one can define for any abelian group ''G'' the minimum quantity <math>EGZ(G)</math> of elements of ''G'' such that there must be a subsequence of <math>o(G)</math> elements (where <math>o(G)</math> is the order of the group) which adds to zero. It is known that <math>EGZ(G)\leq 2o(G) - 1</math>, and that this bound is strict if and only if <math>G = \mathbb{Z}_m</math>.<ref name=":0" />
